project.purpose: Own one bounded Agent Run's durable cognition, provider/tool interaction, action admission, effect binding, recovery, and completion proposal without owning caller Task meaning or Runtime physical truth.

nodes.label: RunContract
nodes.responsibility: Bind one exact Harness Run contract, provider/tool affordances, budgets, and caller context.
acceptance: A run is independently identifiable and bounded.
Run Trace evidence must use exact integer event/version/time/clock fields, string Run identity, and an immutable tuple of events; numeric aliases are rejected at the native consumer boundary.

nodes.label: ContextProjection
nodes.responsibility: Compile current model cognition from durable working set, current ingress, and attempt context rather than replaying complete history.
acceptance: Context can be rebuilt from bounded owned sources.

nodes.label: ActionAdmission
nodes.responsibility: Turn model/tool proposals into exact admitted actions without treating intent as authority.
acceptance: Unadmitted proposals cannot become tool effects.
Bounded native TLC Provider claim admission model checks a current claimant generation and expiry replacement before physical dispatch. Executable SQLite refinement is independently scoped.

nodes.label: EffectBinding
nodes.responsibility: Bind admitted tool intents to physical evidence while preserving ambiguous-effect semantics.
acceptance: Lost response does not cause blind duplicate effect.
Live A/B MemoryRuntime H04 fixture admits only exact requestId-to-digest replay, disjoint edit intervals, and one producer per file; malformed requests cannot emit a successful effect receipt.

Temporal Worker deployment derives four exact runtime package versions solely from the installed requirements freeze, rejects stale/invalid source projections, and evaluates runtimeVersionsExact using one observed interpreter state per Plan.
Finite model separates at-most-one physical Provider effect, durable result, ambiguous outcome and caller acknowledgement. Live delivery is not entailed by TLC PASS.

Durable ConversationRelay SQLite materialization transitions validate the exact post-write receipt before COMMIT; missing or malformed readback must ROLLBACK and fail with CarrierConflict. This contract holds for intent, effect attempt, ordinary outcome, and human-resume claim under Python -O, without claiming external provider atomicity.

A durable Provider completion digest is not caller acknowledgement: native TLC must prove acknowledgement requires fresh or privacy-authorized retained result, and metadata-only redaction remains independently reachable. Concrete SQLite replay/recovery tests and the separately merged #668 12-worker consumer remain required; bounded model PASS alone does not prove implementation refinement.

The Python -O qualification requires executable, non-elided SQL-state postconditions for adverse receipt markers and persisted row standings; two deliberately unequal witnesses must still raise AssertionError in both optimized and standard interpreters. A pytest exit-zero without these checks is not durable receipt proof.

A CFT human-session open must prove the exact durable OPENING reservation receipt inside its SQLite transaction before any systemd.start: deleted or mutated post-insert reservation rolls back and no physical browser start/stop is attempted. Native SQLite adversarial AFTER INSERT triggers cover deleted rows and wrong slot; external browser readiness and deployed installed state require separate evidence. The OPENING-to-ACTIVE transition must additionally prove exact durable ACTIVE receipt after physical readiness, or roll back and compensate the started systemd target rather than return a false READY.

After systemd.stop of an existing human-session, the CFT CLOSED transition must affect the exact selected lifecycle and preserve all immutable session identity fields with an exact closedAtMs. Native SQLite post-UPDATE row removal or reactivation must ROLLBACK and raise SessionConflict, never emit a successful CLOSED receipt; this source invariant does not make systemd.stop and the SQLite write one atomic physical transaction.

Conversation-role adoption and wake-intent Turn identity allocation require exact, typed, post-write SQLite receipt readback before COMMIT; a missing or tampered row must roll back with owner Conflict and must not commit any trigger side effect. Exact replays cannot return a forged provider/session or invalid UUIDv7 turn identity. The physical test scope is the two original SQLite stores, not external provider SEND atomicity.

The Browserless turn-effect SQLite read-only reconciliation path must close its native sqlite3.Connection exactly once for both existing row and absent-table cases; SQLite transaction context is not a connection-lifetime owner. A real tracked sqlite3.Connection subclass is the negative/positive resource oracle; this does not close unrelated connections in other callers.

Until HarnessStore has a PostgreSQL-backed replacement qualified by the same lease, revision, event and receipt consumer tests, SQLite backup verification must bind exact filename identity: reserved #/?/% are physical bytes, never query or fragment syntax; valid-but-wrong database aliases must fail consumer equivalence.

PostgreSQL-first cutover acceptance is consumer equivalence for run/event CAS, leases, unique dedupe and provider receipts under serializable retry, independent data restoration/rollback, production readback and retirement of superseded SQLite authority; a connector or schema alone is not migration.

Migration-source identity: existing Agent Automation Release must snapshot and copy the exact SQLite ledger path through standard-library URI encoding. A literal '#' in a filename or ancestor directory cannot redirect the read to another valid database, and a corrupted named source must never pass by alias. This is interim SQLite source integrity, not PostgreSQL migration completion.

PostgreSQL-first WakeTurn identity cutover: a wakeIntentId maps to exactly one immutable UUIDv7 turnRequestId under native PostgreSQL SERIALIZABLE retry. A previously populated SQLite wake source may be retired only after a quiesced, exclusive-source-lock import proves row-by-row equivalence and installs exact INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE fail-closed triggers. Browserless may use PG only on an explicit DSN, after validating the source seal plus legacy-to-PG identity equality; a missing source requires explicitly qualified fresh bootstrap. Failure must hold without SQLite fallback or provider SEND. This source-level/native PostgreSQL evidence does not prove already-running legacy workers have stopped or an installed deployment has switched.

PostgreSQL WakeTurn first-schema admission is a single serialized database capability: a transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock precedes CREATE SCHEMA/TABLE; on an empty disposable database 12-way cold initialization succeeds without pg_namespace UniqueViolation and creates exactly one schema/table.

Native PostgreSQL WakeTurn first-admission schema is not certified by CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alone: existing relation must be a plain table with the exact six typed nonnull columns, an immutable wake primary key, a nondeferrable unique turn identity and a nonnegative BIGINT timestamp check. The PostgreSQL cutover marker itself also requires a plain two-column non-RLS table with an enforced nondeferrable PRIMARY KEY on cutover_id, preventing multiple contradictory PENDING/ACTIVE marker rows. Disposable PostgreSQL tests falsify an existing same-named table missing unique turn identity, using a wrong timestamp type or missing its check, or a cutover marker table missing its primary key; incomplete schema rejects before any WakeTurn write. This only qualifies the current admission transaction and does not establish arbitrary future DDL noninterference or complete SQLite-to-PostgreSQL cutover.
